For a mean-zero datum and s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s), since |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k| at k!=0. Apply E001 with s=gamma, T_s=T, B0=R and initial homogeneous norm bounded by R. For arbitrary B>0 and two real mean-zero L2 initial data with norm sum <=B, apply E001's L2 existence and two-flow Lipschitz clauses at theta=0, T_s=T. The source twist is unitary, and the same reflection identifies the physical target-sign flows; their normalized L2 distance is unchanged. Thus sup_[0,T]||u-tilde u||_2<=C(T,B)||u0-tilde u0||_2. This includes convergence from Fourier polynomial data, which tend to f0 in L2 by the defining square-summable Fourier norm. The limit agrees with the H^gamma flow by uniqueness, establishing the smooth-approximation convention.

Fix arbitrary smooth real mean-zero datum and integer L>=1. H001 gives tau=T/L>0. N005 ensures all iterates are smooth, real and mean-zero. In E005 set tau_s=tau, t_j=t_n and f=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n.
